Q1: A huge fire (captioned '1666 — The Great Fire', dated 2 Sept 1666) that burns through the crowded old city.
Q2: It starts in one small place. The frames show a baker's oven and a burning house on a narrow street, with the caption 'Thomas Farriner, baker to the King'. A map marks a small area near Pudding Lane and London Bridge. The fire then spreads over days, 2 to 6 Sept, until a large area is burned.
Q3: People flee on foot, carrying bundles. They load carts with belongings and crowd onto boats on the Thames with their goods. Later they camp in open fields in tents. The Lord Mayor is shown, but the pictures do not show him doing anything specific.
Q4: Not sure. The pictures never clearly show the church on the hill. A tall tower stands among the ruins afterwards, but I can't say what happened to the church itself.
Q5: The city is rebuilt in red brick. Builders on scaffolds are shown, along with a surveyor and officials with plans. A plan engraved in 1767 and a surveyor staking out ground suggest the old street layout was largely kept. The streets in the aerial views look much the same as before the fire, though they are widened and straightened in places. The pictures don't clearly say whether a new grid was proposed or rejected.
Q6: A large white domed cathedral with towers (labelled '1711 — The dome rules the skyline', with a height marker of 365 ft). A tall free-standing column appears at about 1673–75 with a height marker of 202 ft; an engraving labelled 'The Monument' is shown beside it.
Q7: On 29–30 Dec 1940 the city burns again, and the caption calls it 'The second great fire'. Airships or balloons hang over the street, firefighters work with hoses, and a '100,000 incendiaries' counter appears. The white domed cathedral still stands lit by flames, so it survives. A large area in the middle is flattened (highlighted in orange) and is rebuilt afterwards.
Q8: A modern 2026 city of glass towers and concrete blocks, with the Thames, bridges and a lit-up night view. The domed cathedral is still visible among the towers.
